doc.title: Joe Segal — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Only child, a failed year of trombone, and his neighborhood
summary: He has no siblings, takes up trombone because his mother vetoed drums, and lives in the Logan section of Philadelphia.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: Kind of going back here, do you have any siblings?
And did you early on have any music lessons there, or, besides your father taking you and exposing you to these wonderful bands...

Well I wanted to play drums, and I’d still like to play drums, but I don’t have much talent for it. But my mother said no because we lived like in a basement apartment. She was afraid it would break our lease and make noise. So I settled on the trombone because Tommy Dorsey was the big thing. So I took a year of that with a great trombonist from the Jan Savitt band, and took a year, and I couldn’t remember where anything went with the trombone, so that was that. I never could play it. But I had an old King that I hauled around with me when I went with the army until somebody stole it, and that was fine with me.
So what neighborhood did you live in in Philly?

I lived in what they called Logan. It’s 4800 North. When I was about ten I started traveling the city myself on the subway and so forth. Because being an only child and my mother working all day I had to get around by myself. So that was good.
